sections.h2: Billings neighborhoods and why they matter
sections.html:
Billings lies in the Yellowstone Valley at 3,126 feet, and sandstone cliffs known as the Rims (or Rimrocks) run through town. They curve north and east of downtown, which is what separates it from the Heights and from Lockwood. The city's 2025 population estimate is 121,239.

  • Downtown and the valley floor: older housing close to the Yellowstone River.
  • Billings Heights: north of the Rims along U.S. Highway 87, which becomes Main Street inside the city.
  • Lockwood: east of downtown.
  • South Hills, West End and Shiloh: reached from Interstate 90 and Montana Highway 3.

Rim views and quick access to the trails along the cliffs are selling points worth naming in a listing. Healthcare employs more people than any other sector here, with Billings Clinic at about 4,500 workers and St. Vincent Regional Hospital at about 2,200, so hospital staff are a regular part of the buyer pool.

Summers in Billings run hot and dry, and winters run cold and dry. Snowfall totals 57.4 inches in an average year, but chinook winds melt much of it quickly. Hail is what drives roof inspections. On June 20, 2010, a tornado brought hail up to golf ball size through the Heights and downtown.

If your shingles are old, a buyer's inspector will likely say so, and a repair request can hold up a mortgage-backed closing. Plenty of owners with tired roofs sell as is. That avoids the repair back and forth, and the offer simply reflects what the house needs.

sections.h2: Property tax in Billings and Yellowstone County
sections.html:
The Yellowstone County Treasurer handles Billings tax bills from 2825 3rd Avenue North, Room 113. The phone number is 406-256-2802. Real estate payments follow the state calendar, with a one-time shift in this cycle.

Real estate paymentYellowstone County date
First halfNovember 30 (2026 only: December 3)
Second halfMay 31 (2027 only: June 1)
Deadline time5 p.m. Mountain Time, next business day if a weekend or holiday
Late payment2% penalty and 5/6 of 1% interest per month

The state's 2026 rates give a lived-in home or long-term rental a tiered scale that starts at 0.76% on the first $378,000 of value. A second home, short-term rental or vacant lot costs a flat 1.90%.

Think the valuation is off? You get 30 days from the notice date. File Form AB-26 with the Department of Revenue, or take the appeal straight to the county tax appeal board.

sections.h2: Three ways to sell in Billings
sections.html:
Most owners weigh an agent listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. Their costs, timelines and risks differ.

  • Agent listing: more buyers see the house, but you pay commission and deal with showings and any repairs an inspection turns up.
  • Sale by owner: no commission, though marketing, the contract and the paperwork fall to you.
  • Cash offer: a direct purchase, usually as is, closing on a date you pick.

Every route ends the same way. A notary acknowledges the deed, the county clerk and recorder records it with a Realty Transfer Certificate, and the recording fee is $20 for the first page plus $10 for each page after. Property tax owed on the house is a lien, and closing pays it.

Want a cash offer for a Billings house? Describe the property in the form above. A written offer comes back to you, and declining it costs nothing.

Tell us the address and a few details through the form on this page. We look at the house and the title, then send a written offer. Take your time with it. You can accept, counter or walk away, and you owe nothing for asking. If you accept, a title company opens the file, confirms who owns the house and lists every lien, including any unpaid property tax. You pick the closing date, within reason, and the deed and Realty Transfer Certificate are recorded with the county clerk and recorder. Funds then go to you after the payoff of any loan or tax.

No repair list, no showings and no waiting on a lender's underwriter. What you give up is the broader competition a listing creates, which is why a written comparison matters.

sections.h2: What goes in the closing file
sections.html:
Plan on a deed, a Realty Transfer Certificate and the recording fee, all going to the county clerk and recorder. The certificate gathers sale prices that the Department of Revenue uses to appraise Montana real property in bulk, so the price you report can influence how nearby homes are valued later.

  • Names of seller and buyer should read the same on the certificate and the deed.
  • The last four digits of each party's Social Security or employer identification number are required.
  • A notary has to acknowledge the deed before it can be recorded.

A recorded deed puts later buyers and lenders on notice from the moment it is filed.

sections.h2: Before you decide, a short checklist
sections.html:
Start with the latest tax statement and see whether the first half is paid. If the amount or due date is unclear, call the county treasurer, since the 2026 and 2027 dates move by a few days. Walk the roof, because hail is the most frequent inspection topic. Then decide whether you want the wide exposure of a listing or the speed of a cash sale. If any lien exists, mention it to the title company at the start so a payoff figure is ready on signing day.

A cash sale as is cuts out the lender's appraisal, the repair requests and the wait for loan approval. Because the offer reflects the house's condition, compare it in writing with what you would net from a listing after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Ask any buyer how the title work will be handled, who pays the recording costs and what date the funds arrive.

If you owned the home as a rental, short-term or long-term, say so up front. The rate class affects what the buyer will pay in tax next year, and a buyer who plans to live there can apply for the lower homestead scale.

faqs.q: When are Yellowstone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half of real estate tax is due November 30, with December 3 as the 2026 date, and the second half is due May 31, with June 1 in 2027. Payments are due by 5 p.m. Mountain Time.

faqs.q: What rate applies to a Billings primary residence in 2026?
faqs.a: A tiered rate that begins at 0.76% on the first $378,000 of value. Second homes, short-term rentals and vacant lots pay a flat 1.90%.
Yes. A June 20, 2010 tornado came with hail up to golf ball size and damaged downtown, the Heights and the MetraPark Arena. Roof condition is a common point in a Billings sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Billings house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a Billings house in its present condition, and the sale still requires a recorded deed and a Realty Transfer Certificate.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Billings?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $20 for the first page and $10 for each added page, paid to the county clerk and recorder when the deed and certificate are filed.
